Title: Unsubsidised petrol, diesel prices rise 25 sen - MOF
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 petrol and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 25 sen per litre for the period from Sept 10 to 16.
The Finance Ministry (MOF), in a statement today, said RON97 would be priced at RM4.50 per litre from RM4.25 previously, while RON95 would rise to RM4.02 from RM3.77 and unsubsidised diesel to RM4.92 from RM4.67.
MOF said global crude oil prices rose significantly during the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period following renewed escalation in the conflict between the United States and Iran and increased risks of disruption to petroleum supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.
"Brent crude oil prices rose throughout the APM calculation period before reaching US$97.31 a barrel on Monday. Geopolitical risk premiums on global oil supplies also increased following continued retaliatory attacks between the United States and Iran.
"At the same time, the global market for refined petroleum products remained tight. Disruptions to refining capacity in West Asia and continued attacks on Russian refineries have reduced supplies of petrol, diesel and other petroleum products to international markets," it said.
MOF said diesel prices in the international market also rose faster than crude oil prices due to constraints on refining capacity and declining inventories.
"After 193 days of conflict in West Asia, petroleum flows through the Strait of Hormuz and global refining capacity have yet to return to normal. If this situation persists, declining inventories and increasingly tight supplies of refined petroleum products could increase risk premiums on global petrol and diesel prices," MOF said.
The ministry said the Madani Government would continue to protect the people and businesses from the impact of global uncertainties by maintaining targeted BUDI Madani subsidies for eligible consumers.
Under BUDI95, eligible recipients will continue to pay RM1.99 per litre for RON95, with the Government bearing a subsidy of RM2.03 per litre, or 50 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM4.02.
For BUDI Diesel, recipients will pay RM2.10 per litre, with the Government providing a subsidy of RM2.82 per litre, or 57 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM4.92.
Meanwhile, petrol prices under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and diesel prices under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) will remain at RM2.05 and RM2.15 per litre, respectively.
The basic monthly eligibility limit for BUDI95 and BUDI Diesel had been raised again to 300 litres from Sept 1, while eligible owners of diesel-powered pickup trucks and jeeps would receive an additional 100 litres, bringing their total monthly eligibility to 400 litres, the minitsry added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore's DBS sued for US$1bil in 1MDB-linked claim
Article:
SINGAPORE: Liquidators of four companies linked to global 1Malaysia Development Berhad recovery efforts have sued DBS Bank, seeking an estimated S$1.298 billion (US$1.03 billion) in damages, Southeast Asia's largest lender DBS said on Wednesday.
DBS rejected the claim and said it would fight it vigorously, adding that the company has made no provision for the lawsuit.

Title: BN must not be complacent after Johor, Negri Sembilan victories
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional's victories in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections should not make the coalition complacent, but instead spur it to continue working to maintain the people's confidence.
Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said party members must take seriously the message delivered by Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi during his briefing and work to convince the people of BN's capabilities.
He said Umno and BN must also learn from their past weaknesses and make improvements to ensure the coalition continues to earn the people's trust.
"We won Johor and we won Negri Sembilan, but that does not mean we can win forever.
"So, we must not be arrogant. We must continue working," he said when met after the Umno presidential briefing at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here.
Meanwhile, Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin described the presidential briefing as a reminder to all party members not to take the victories in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections for granted.
He said the victories should not create a sense of complacency among party members, but instead serve as a catalyst to further strengthen the party.
"So that we do not take it as something that makes us feel comfortable. It is important for us to continue building the party, strengthening the party and ensuring that the party continues to gain the confidence of the people," he said.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said Zahid had also urged all Umno members at the grassroots, branch and division levels, as well as the top leadership, to remain united and not become divided.
He said the briefing focused on the party's direction, particularly efforts to strengthen Umno in facing any challenges and the possibility of facing the next general election and state polls.
"Umno now has very good momentum following its victories in two states, which has also given the party a boost as it prepares to face any possibilities in the future," he said.

Title: Azeez lawyer disputes claim over lock-up attire, handcuffs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The lawyer for former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim denied that his client had chosen to wear a purple lock-up shirt and handcuffs when he appeared in court.
Counsel Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad said police had instructed Azeez to change into the lock-up attire shortly before the remand proceedings.
"We are instructed by our client that, prior to leaving the police lock-up, he had initially been permitted to wear his normal clothing.
"However, shortly before he was brought out of the lock-up, he was instructed to change into the purple lock-up attire in compliance with the police standard operating procedures," he said in a statement today.
Amer said Azeez was then brought before the Sessions Court (Criminal) 2 for the police's remand application, where a two-day remand order was granted.
He said Azeez remained under police custody and control at all material times, adding that the handcuffs placed on him were also put on by police and not the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
"Following the remand proceedings, our client was brought directly from the Sessions Court (Criminal) 2 to the Sessions Court (Criminal) 9 for the MACC charge against him to be read.
"Throughout this entire period, including his transfer from one courtroom to the other, our client remained under police custody.
"He was not released from police custody in between the two proceedings, nor was he given any opportunity to change out of the lock-up attire before being brought before the Sessions Court (Criminal) 9," he said.
Amer said Azeez's appearance in the purple lock-up attire and handcuffs during the subsequent MACC proceedings was therefore not a matter of personal choice.
"We are therefore flabbergasted by the statement attributed to the MACC suggesting that our client had chosen or insisted upon wearing the lock-up attire and handcuffs.
"For the avoidance of doubt, our client was under police custody throughout, and the lock-up attire and handcuffs concerned arose in the course of that police custody," he said.
He said any suggestion that Azeez had voluntarily chosen to appear in that manner was incorrect and gave a misleading impression of the circumstances in which he was brought before the court.
Earlier today, MACC said Azeez had chosen to appear in court wearing a police lock-up uniform and handcuffs despite being advised that he did not have to do so.

Title: King, Queen mourn five killed in Sarawak helicopter crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, and Raja Permaisuri Agong Raja Zarith Sofiah, the Queen of Malaysia, have expressed their condolences to the families of those killed in the helicopter crash in Sarawak yesterday.
Their Majesties prayed that the families and next of kin of the victims, which include a pilot and Health Ministry personnel, would be granted strength and fortitude in facing the loss of their loved ones.
"Al-Fatihah, and my condolences to all the family members of the victims.
"Their service and sacrifice will always be remembered," Sultan Ibrahim said in a statement on Facebook today.
[[nid:1529225]]
Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, the Sultan of Pahang, and Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, also conveyed their condolences to the families of the five victims who died in the crash.
Their Royal Highnesses expressed their deepest sorrow and prayed that all arrangements for the victims' remains would proceed smoothly and that operations by the authorities would be carried out safely.
They also hoped the victims' families would be granted strength, fortitude and patience.
Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM)
said that a helicopter carrying five people
, including its pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing (STOL) port in Sarawak.
Those killed include Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, Dr. Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, Alexson Adit, Debra Moset and Jessie Paya.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former subsidiary CEO remanded four more days over corruption probe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The remand of a former chief executive officer (CEO) of a subsidiary of a federal statutory body has been extended by four days to assist investigations into alleged misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving the appointment of a developer for a project in Kuala Lumpur.
A source said the remand order, which runs from tomorrow until Sept 13, was issued by Magistrate Ezrene Zakaria after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) made the application at the Putrajaya Magistrate's Court here this morning.
"The remand application was made after the suspect's initial remand period ended today. The suspect was previously remanded for three days from last Monday," the source said.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, said the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009.
Last Monday, MACC obtained a five-day remand order until Sept 11 against two individuals, including a Datuk who is also a former director-general of the statutory body, while the former CEO, who is currently receiving treatment at Putrajaya Hospital, was remanded for three days until today.
The two individuals, in their 50s and 60s, were detained last Sunday after appearing at the MACC headquarters to have their statements recorded.
MACC has opened seven investigation papers into allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia Airlines arranges flights, reimbursements after MH4 diversion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines has arranged additional flights and reimbursements for passengers affected by a UK air traffic control disruption that resulted in flight MH4 being diverted to Manchester.
In a travel advisory today, the carrier said it would operate additional flights MH4D (Manchester to London Heathrow) and MH1D (London Heathrow to Kuala Lumpur) to get affected passengers to their final destinations.
Due to limited hotel availability across UK airports, the airline advised passengers to book their own accommodation.
It said it would reimburse room costs of up to £150 (RM821) per night, as well as reasonable meal expenses and local transport, provided passengers retained itemised receipts.
Stand-up comedian Dr Jason Leong has criticised Malaysia Airlines' crisis management team after Flight MH4 from Kuala Lumpur to London Heathrow was diverted to Manchester Airport, leaving passengers and flight crew without ground support.
In a video posted on his Facebook page, Leong said the aircraft was diverted to Manchester due to operational closures at London Heathrow.
He said passengers were left sitting in the baggage reclaim area for hours without information about their luggage, hotel accommodation or onward transport.
Leong said there was no carousel number, no luggage coming out and no Malaysia Airlines ground representative at the airport to assist passengers or provide instructions.
He also criticised the airline's crisis management team for failing to provide logistical support, saying the flight attendants and pilots were also left without hotel accommodation or transport.
Leong said the flight captain was forced to manage frustrated passengers directly in the terminal.
On luggage delays at Manchester Airport, Malaysia Airlines urged passengers to proceed to their accommodation without waiting for their checked bags, citing safety constraints caused by stand congestion and remote parking.
The airline said all checked baggage remained secure and would be transported to London Heathrow on flight MH4D.
Passengers who need to repurchase essential medication because of missing baggage can submit their receipts for full reimbursement.

Title: RTD backs MACC action over fake vehicle ownership documents
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Road Transport Department (RTD) has thrown its full support behind the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) action over suspected falsification of documents for vehicle ownership transfers.
RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the department would give its full cooperation to MACC and leave the matter to the commission.
"We will continue to strengthen cooperation between MACC and RTD, particularly in information sharing, the prevention of corruption and misconduct, as well as efforts to enhance integrity and governance within the department," he said in a statement today.
Aedy said RTD remained open to working with MACC to identify any weaknesses or loopholes that could create opportunities for irregularities or abuse of its systems, before implementing appropriate improvements.
He stressed that the department would not tolerate or compromise with any party that exploited, abused their authority or betrayed the trust placed in them for personal gain.
He said the firm stance was in line with RTD's commitment to ensuring transparent, accountable and integrity-based enforcement governance.
Aedy said RTD remained committed to carrying out enforcement professionally in the interest of road safety and the public.
"Any breach of integrity will be dealt with firmly in accordance with the laws and regulations in force," he said.
It was reported that
11 people, including six civil servants,
have been remanded to assist investigations into an alleged syndicate involved in submitting falsified documents for vehicle ownership transfers.
The suspects, comprising seven men and four women aged between 30 and 40, were brought before magistrate Norizan Riduan today.
Norizan allowed the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC)'s application to remand the suspects from today until Monday.
The remand was sought to facilitate investigations under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno to let top leadership decide GE16 electoral cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The decision on seat allocations and Umno's partners for the 16th General Election (GE16) will be determined by the party's top leadership.
Umno Information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said this was among the messages conveyed by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi during the presidential briefing held in conjunction with the 2026 Umno general assembly today.
"Zahid also mentioned that decisions on party matters must be left to the top party leadership to determine seat allocations and election partners.
"And we also acknowledge that the states and the federal level are different," she told reporters here today.
Azalina said the "blue wave" could now be seen as an increasingly clear reality, but efforts to unite party members must remain a priority.
"We can see that the blue wave is indeed becoming a reality.
"But more importantly, we need to get party members to unite and remain focused," she said.
She said the party's wings were also expected to take guidance from the president's message to ensure the party's focus and unity were strengthened ahead of GE16.
Meanwhile, Negeri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said the message delivered by the president could be regarded as important guidance and a mandate for the party to face the upcoming elections, including the Melaka state election.
"The president gave us very important guidance and a mandate for us to face the days and future ahead, particularly for the resurgence of Umno and Barisan Nasional.
"Not only for the Melaka election, but also for us to face elections in other states, including GE16," he said.
He said it was not impossible for Umno and BN to repeat the major victories achieved in Johor and Negri Sembilan, provided there was solidarity and unity among the party's election machinery and leaders at all levels.
He said such unity must be embraced by all party members to ensure Umno could rise again and achieve success in the coming elections.
"It is not impossible for us to repeat our major victories in Johor and Negri Sembilan, provided there is solidarity and unity among the election machinery and Umno leaders at all levels.
"If this can be adopted as a guiding principle and lesson, Umno will rise again at all levels and victory will be on Umno's side, particularly with the blue wave at all levels," he said.
Former Pasir Salak member of Parliament Datuk Seri Tajuddin Abdul Rahman said Zahid had also hinted at the possibility of forging cooperation with parties that had previously been his political adversaries.
"The president did give a hint (about cooperation). Perhaps Umno will choose people who were previously our enemies, and we can make peace with them again.
"People who were previously friendly with us may no longer be able to be friendly or cooperate with us.
"Yes, that is a possibility. But it is not tied to any particular party. Everyone can think about it for themselves," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KLK's scion Lee Jia Zhang to take over the mantle starting Oct 1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) has appointed its chief operating officer Lee Jia Zhang as chief executive officer (CEO), effective Oct 1.
Lee, 43, will succeed his father, executive chairman Tan Sri Lee Oi Hian, who served as KLK's CEO for more than three decades.
Oi Hian was appointed group chairman and CEO in 1993 and stepped down as the chairman in 2008, but remained CEO until February 2024.
He was then redesignated executive chairman, while Jia Zhang continued to oversee the company's day-to-day operations as COO.
In a statement, KLK said the appointment is part of its orderly leadership transition and is aimed at ensuring continuity in the company's strategic and operational direction.
Jia Zhang, who joined KLK in 2010, has held various leadership roles across the company's plantation, oleochemical, refinery, property and corporate businesses.
He was appointed to KLK's board as executive director in May 2018 and became COO in October 2021.
He previously served as managing director of Palm-Oleo Sdn Bhd from January 2017 to December 2018 and CEO of KLK OLEO from April 2022 to September 2024.
Before joining KLK, Jia Zhang held audit roles at Ernst & Young in the United Kingdom and KPMG in Kuala Lumpur.
He is currently chairman of the Asean Oleochemical Manufacturers Group, secretary and council member of the Malaysian Palm Oil Association, and a member of the board of trustees of the Malaysian Palm Oil Council.
Jia Zhang holds a master's degree with honours in chemical engineering from Imperial College London and is a chartered accountant and member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Scotland.
Oi Hian said the board was confident that Lee would build on the company's foundations and lead it towards sustained growth.
"We have full confidence that he will build on the strength of the group laid over decades and take KLK towards robust and sustained growth as well as our vision of becoming a globally recognised agri-based organisation, with aspiration to be a beacon of our industry," he said.

Title: Bursa reprimands Techna-X over delay in annual report, audit adjustments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd has publicly reprimanded Techna-X Bhd for breaching Main Market listing requirements over the delayed issuance of its annual report and failure to reflect audit adjustments in its quarterly financial results.
The regulator said Techna-X failed to issue its annual report for the 18-month financial period ended Dec 31, 2025 by the April 30, 2026 deadline.
The report was issued on May 8, 2026, representing a delay of five market days.
Bursa Malaysia also found that Techna-X's sixth quarterly report for the period ended Dec 31, 2025, announced on Feb 27, 2026, did not take into account adjustments subsequently identified in the audited financial statements.
The regulator said Techna-X had reported an unaudited loss attributable to owners of the company of RM23.58 million in the quarterly report, compared with an audited loss of RM29.25 million in its annual financial statements.
This represented a difference of RM5.677 million, or 24.1 per cent.
Techna-X had said the deviation was due to additional audit adjustments, including impairment losses on other receivables, amounts owing from associates and intangible assets, as well as accounting adjustments arising from the waiver of debts owed to directors of a subsidiary.
Bursa Malaysia said the circumstances giving rise to the adjustments already existed when the quarterly report was prepared.
"Hence, there was no reasonable change in circumstances and Techna-X could not rely on the finalisation of the audit or external auditors' recommendations to justify its failure to take into account the adjustments," it said in a statement.
The regulator said the delay in the annual report was mainly due to Techna-X's failure to maintain or provide the necessary information, documents and accounting records to its external auditors to complete the audit within the stipulated timeframe.
Although the delay was five market days, Bursa Malaysia said investors were deprived of the company's audited financial information for an extended period of more than 18 months.
As part of the enforcement action, Techna-X has been required to have its quarterly report submissions undergo a limited review by its external auditors for four quarters, beginning no later than the financial period ending Sept 30, 2026.
The company must also ensure its directors and relevant personnel attend training on compliance with the Main Market Listing Requirements, particularly financial statement requirements.
Its board must further review and assess the adequacy and competency of its finance and accounting resources, as well as the adequacy and effectiveness of its financial reporting policies and procedures.
Bursa Malaysia said it had not found any of Techna-X's directors to have caused or permitted the breaches.
However, it reminded the board that directors have a duty to maintain appropriate standards of responsibility and accountability in ensuring compliance with listing requirements.
"Bursa Malaysia views the breaches seriously and has reminded Techna-X and its board of their responsibilities to maintain the appropriate standards of corporate responsibility and accountability to its shareholders and the investing public and ensure that such breaches do not recur," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EI Power to acquire Shah Alam factory for RM17mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: EI Power Bhd's unit EI Power Technologies Sdn Bhd is acquiring a freehold factory in Shah Alam for RM17.2 million, mainly funded by proceeds from its initial public offering (IPO).
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the subsidiary had entered into a sale and purchase agreement with Elitesoft Asia Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of the two-and-a-half-storey semi-detached factory.
The property sits on 16,100 square feet (sq ft) of freehold industrial land and has a built-up area of about 17,472 sq ft.
EI Power said the purchase price was arrived at on a willing-buyer, willing-seller basis, taking into account the property's location and an independent valuation of RM17.3 million by IM Global Property Consultants Sdn Bhd.
RM15 million of the consideration will be paid from its IPO proceeds, while the remaining RM2.2 million will come from internal funds, EI Power said in the filing.
The company also plans to carry out renovation and fit-out works, with up to RM3.3 million of IPO proceeds to be used for the works.
EI Power was listed on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia on May 21, 2026.
The company currently operates from rented office and storage premises in Selangor.
It said the acquisition would provide additional office and warehouse capacity to support its growing workforce, storage requirements and operations, while catering for its evolving business needs.
The property is located in an established industrial area with access to major highways, which the company said would improve accessibility to its customers and suppliers and support operational efficiency.
"The strategic location and additional office and warehouse capacity are expected to enhance the group's operational efficiency and provide the necessary infrastructure to support its long-term business growth and expansion," it said.
The property also has an existing rooftop tenancy with a Malaysian telecommunications infrastructure provider that generates RM6,000 in monthly rental income and expires on May 31, 2027. The tenancy and rental income will be transferred to EI Power Technologies upon handover.
EI Power said the acquisition is not expected to have any material effect on the group's net assets, net asset value per share or gearing, or its earnings and earnings per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026.
The acquisition is expected to be completed within three months from the date of the sale and purchase agreement, with a one-month extension.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Zahid denies attending meeting linked to Negri Sembilan royal dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied attending a meeting where Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim signed a proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state ruler.
"I was not there. He (Ismail) has already denied that I was there," he told reporters here today.
Zahid said Umno respected the royal institution, the institution of the Undang and Negri Sembilan's customs.
Earlier, Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki also
denied attending the meeting
.
Azalina said she was not present when the proclamation was signed, while Asyraf said he was not involved and was only part of the party's national leadership.
The proclamation is at the centre of a
royal dispute
in Negri Sembilan, with Ismail claiming he had been pressured into signing the document to remove Tuanku Muhriz as the state's Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Ismail said he had lodged a police report at 6pm yesterday.
He said the state government's position was that the document did not comply with the processes and procedures under Article 10 of the state constitution and was therefore invalid and unenforceable.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Zahid denies receiving resignation letter from Negri Sembilan MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today denied receiving a resignation letter from Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
"No, there's none," he said briefly when asked by reporters here whether Ismail had handed him a resignation letter.
The question arose amid the state's royal dispute involving a proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Negri Sembilan's Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Earlier, Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said he was unaware of speculation surrounding Ismail's resignation.
Jalaluddin said he was no longer part of the state administration and had learnt of developments through media reports.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ENRA in pre-joint bidding cooperation with China Offshore for FSO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ENRA Group Bhd's indirect subsidiary Hexagon Energy Logistics Sdn Bhd has entered into a pre-joint bidding cooperation agreement with China Offshore Engineering & Technology Co Ltd to jointly bid for a floating storage and offloading (FSO) project in Southeast Asia.
In a bourse filing, ENRA said Hexagon and China Offshore intend to work exclusively with each other to prepare and submit a joint bid for the upcoming tender involving the provision of an FSO solution in the region.
China Offshore is involved in providing integrated solutions for the oil and gas, decarbonisation, renewable energy, deepwater mining and other ocean resources sectors.
The parties will negotiate the specific scope of work, pricing and responsibilities once the official tender documents are issued, before formalising the arrangements under a separate definitive agreement.
ENRA said the agreement serves as a non-binding framework and does not create any financial obligations at this stage.
The agreement will remain effective until a definitive agreement is signed, the project is cancelled, or both parties mutually agree to discontinue their pursuit of the project.
ENRA said the agreement is not expected to have any immediate material impact on its earnings, net assets or gearing for the financial year ending March 31, 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] 'Who forced him?' Zahid asks over Negri MB's coercion claim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has questioned who allegedly forced Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to sign a proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state ruler.
"Who forced him?" he said when asked by reporters here today about Ismail's claim that he had been pressured into signing the proclamation.
"I think it would be best for the statement to be verified by his own lawyer, if the lawyer was present during the signing of the proclamation," he said.
Zahid was speaking after his presidential briefing at the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here today.
He said Umno respected the royal institution, the institution of the Undang and the customs of Negri Sembilan.
"We will not dirty our hands in dealing with the situation in Negri Sembilan," he said, adding that a press conference on the matter might be held soon
The proclamation is at the centre of a royal dispute in Negri Sembilan, with Ismail claiming he
had been pressured
into signing the document to remove Tuanku Muhriz as the state's Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Ismail said he lodged a police report at about 6pm yesterday to allow the authorities to investigate the matter.
He said the state government considered the document invalid, unconstitutional and unenforceable as it did not comply with the processes and procedures under Article 10 of the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: LFE secures RM24mil worth of jobs in Ara Damansara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: LFE Corp Bhd has secured three contracts worth a combined RM23.87 million for electrical, mechanical and plumbing works at a commercial development in Ara Damansara, Selangor.
Its subsidiary, LFE Engineering Sdn Bhd, accepted the letters of award from Pembinaan Bina Bumi Sdn Bhd to undertake the supply, installation, testing and commissioning works for the redevelopment.
The contracts comprise RM13.3 million for electrical and extra-low-voltage services, RM5.3 million for air-conditioning and mechanical ventilation services, and RM5.27 million for cold and hot water and sanitary plumbing services.
LFE said the contracts have a duration of 27 months, commencing on Dec 22, 2025 and ending on March 21, 2028.
The company expects the contracts to contribute positively to its earnings and net assets per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 and throughout the contract period.

Title: Sirim, NSTP explore consumer awareness on certified products
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Standards and Industrial Research Institute (Sirim) visited Media Prima Berhad at Balai Berita Bangsar here today for an engagement session with New Straits Times Press (NSTP) editors.
The visit aimed to explore the use of Media Prima's platforms to raise awareness among consumers about the importance of purchasing Sirim-certified products.
The initiative aims to help consumers make informed choices when purchasing products, especially through e-commerce platforms, and reduce the risks associated with using non-certified products.
The delegation was led by Sirim's Covering Chief Conformity Assessment Officer, Fauziah Fadzil, and General Manager of Corporate Communications, Shanizar Ahmad Shahar.
NSTP was represented by Associate Editor (Content and Digital) Ahmad Najmuddin Ahmad Najib, while Media Prima Omnia Government Unit General Manager Shanaz Md Azli was also present.
[[nid:1529170]]
Fauziah added that Sirim was planning to engage with e-commerce sellers to discuss the importance of ensuring products sold online comply with Sirim's certification requirements.
"We want to help e-commerce sellers, but at the same time, we want to protect consumers," she said.
The corporate visit is part of Sirim's broader efforts to promote greater awareness of product certification requirements and safety standards among sellers, while encouraging consumers to adopt responsible online shopping.
Towards the end of the visit, the delegation was taken on a tour of the NSTP newsroom, where they were briefed on daily editorial operations and digital publishing activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit ends easier against US dollar as Middle East conflict weighs on sentiment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended easier against the US dollar on Wednesday, as market sentiment remained cautious amid an evolving outlook in Middle East, said an economist.
At 6pm, the local currency eased to 4.0670/0720 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0605/0640.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Brent crude prices hit the psychological level of US$100 a barrel today as the conflict between US-Israel and Iran continues, leading to uncertainties over crude oil supplies from the Gulf region.
"All this suggests a risk of an elevated inflation rate induced by the higher energy prices, which would result in a tighter monetary policy stance by the United States Federal Reserve and Bank of Japan next week.
"Against this backdrop, the US consumer price index (CPI) print, which will be released on Friday, will be the key data point to watch," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said consensus estimates are pencilling in headline inflation at 3.4 per cent for August (July: 3.4 per cent), while core CPI is expected to come in at 2.4 per cent, slightly lower than 2.5 per cent in July.
At the close, the ringgit was lower against a basket of major currencies.
It slipped against the euro to 4.7275/7333 from Tuesday's 4.7151/7191, weakened against the British pound to 5.5043/5110 from 5.4926/4974, and declined against the Japanese yen to 2.6474/6509 from 2.6374/6398.
The ringgit also traded lower against the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.52 from 6.48/6.49 on Tuesday and lost against the Singapore dollar to 3.2150/2192 from 3.2073/2104.
It fell against the Thai baht to 12.3579/3788 from 12.3285/3447 and weakened against the Indonesian rupiah to 232.2/232.6 from 230.3/230.5 at the previous close.

Title: Kuwait Petroleum offering ship-to-ship transfers outside Hormuz to buyers
Article:
SINGAPORE: Kuwait Petroleum Corp is offering the option of ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz to its buyers for safe transportation to final destinations, a company official said on Wednesday.
"Whenever it is safe, we are passing some ships through the Strait of Hormuz and we are giving options to do STS (ship-to-ship) operations outside the Strait of Hormuz," Emad A M Al-Kandari, deputy managing director of International Marketing at Kuwait Petroleum Corp, said at the APPEC industry conference.
Al-Kandari did not specify which petroleum products were sold under STS operations.
The company recently offered naphtha on a delivered ex-ship basis in a handful of tenders in August and September, documents reviewed by Reuters showed.
Some of its cargoes were sold at premiums of up to US$60 per ton to Japan quotes on a delivered basis, market sources said.
KPC typically offered naphtha on a free-on-board basis before the US-Iran war started.
It resumed cargo offers in June for the first time since the war began in February.
Kuwait exported about 200,000 barrels per day of naphtha on average in the first two months of this year, which tanked to zero in April, data from shiptracker Kpler showed.
Its exports in the last two months have remained half of pre-war levels.

Title: Argentina's corn exports set for record as war in Ukraine, European heat wave reshape trade
Article:
BUENOS AIRES: Argentina's corn exports are expected to reach a record 10 million metric tons in August and September, driven by a bumper harvest and strong international demand as buyers seek alternatives to Ukrainian supplies disrupted by war and European crops battered by extreme heat.
The world's third-largest corn exporter is wrapping up its 2025/26 harvest, estimated at 71.70 million tons, nearly 20 per cent above the previous record set five years ago, according to government data.
"Argentine corn right now is very competitive in price and in volume," Gustavo Idigoras, head of the CIARA-CEC grains exporters and crushers chamber, told Reuters. Normal export volumes for August-September typically reach about 3 million tons, he added.
Idigoras said demand from North African countries — typically buyers of Ukrainian grain — has been the primary driver.
"In the last months we've had meetings with several North African countries, who want to have deeper commercial ties with Argentine exporters," he said, without naming specific countries.
Data from Argentina's statistics agency INDEC shows corn shipments to North Africa rose 45 per cent in the first seven months of 2026, to 6.50 million tons, compared with overall export growth of 15 per cent during the same period.
Morocco led the surge, with imports of Argentine corn jumping 133 per cent year-on-year to 1.55 million tons.
Egypt followed with a 48 per cent increase to 2.40 million, while Algerian imports grew 10 per cent to 2.40 million tons.
BLACK SEA BOTTLENECK
The trade shift comes as Russia has intensified strikes on export infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, home to the country's main Black Sea ports.
The attacks have effectively blocked seaports that once handled 90 per cent of Ukraine's grain exports, forcing Kyiv to divert cargo through lower-capacity Danube River ports.
But drought and record heat waves across Europe have drained water levels along the already congested Danube, further constraining Ukrainian shipments, which dropped 52 per cent last month.
"Today, the only way Ukraine can move its production is (over) land. It will very probably end up in Europe, in France, where the heat wave has thrashed corn yields," said Javier Preciado Patiño, an analyst and former trade secretary for Argentina. He said Ukraine's overseas markets are up for grabs.
BRAZILIAN BACKDROP
Argentina's export surge also reflects shifting dynamics in neighbouring Brazil, the world's second-largest corn exporter.
Brazilian shipments have fallen nearly 20 per cent from a record 53 million tons over the past three years, according to US Department of Agriculture data.
That drop has worked to Argentina's advantage, Idigoras said.
Much of the corn that exporters would have loaded at ports such as Santos or Itaqui is instead supplying Brazil's booming ethanol industry, made up of over 300 production units running on sugar or corn.
Dante Romano, research manager for Rosario-based grains broker Max Agro, said Brazil's domestic demand for corn was "impressive" and growing each year.
According to the USDA, Brazil's corn consumption increased 7.10 per cent in 2025/26 to 98 million tons on a season-to-season basis.
"This is important for Argentina because Brazil is a strong corn market competitor, and less corn there for shipping means better commercial opportunities for Argentine exporters," added Romano.

Title: [UPDATED] Man found bound in septic tank at Nibong Tebal house
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: A foul stench from a house in Taman Seri Bistari here led to the discovery of a man's body in a septic tank today.
Police had earlier received a missing person's report from the victim's family in the Seberang Prai Tengah district.
The victim, believed to be in his 50s, was found with his hands and feet bound inside the septic tank at the rear of a single-storey terrace house in Lorong 7, near the kitchen.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim, when contacted, confirmed the incident.
Police were alerted by neighbours who noticed the foul smell coming from the house before conducting an inspection of the premises.
The body, believed to have been in the septic tank for two days, was subsequently removed by police with the assistance of firefighters.
The victim's nephew had also lodged a report after discovering that RM30,000 had been transferred from the victim's bank account to an account belonging to a grocery shop in Sungai Bakap on Sept 7.
Checks reportedly found that the grocery shop owner had been instructed to transfer the money to a bank in Myanmar.
A police report lodged at the Sungai Bakap police station on Sept 8 also detailed earlier suspicious transactions involving the victim's account, including transfers to a business account and a personal account.
Police are investigating the victim's death, the alleged financial transactions and the motive.

Title: EM stocks near highs as Asia tech rallies, but Brent's breach of US$100 clouds sentiment
Article:
NEW YORK: An index tracking global emerging-market stocks hovered around multi-month highs on Wednesday, largely powered by gains in tech-heavy Asian bourses, while surging oil prices kept broader risk appetite in check ahead of US economic data.
The MSCI's EM stocks gauge gained zero point three per cent and was trading near two-month highs.
South Korea's tech-laden KOSPI gained, with chipmaker SK Hynix rising three point five per cent, tracking a renewed bout of interest for AI stocks. Regional peer Taiwan also added zero point two per cent.
Benchmark Brent crude oil futures rose past US$100 a barrel, breaching the symbolic barrier for the first time since Jul 24 as intensifying conflict in the Middle East fuelled growing concern about oil flows from the region.
"Risk appetite remains weak as rising oil prices occupy the headline," said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote.
"Summer was full of hope that a peace agreement could be achieved. This optimism is fading as we enter September."
Elevated energy costs stemming from the conflict have pushed policymakers globally to reassess their monetary policy stances.
Markets will also await the US consumer price data on Friday to gather cues on the Federal Reserve's policy outlook when it meets next week.
Traders currently price in a 60.40 per cent probability that the Fed will hike interest rates at its September meeting, up from a 44.40 per cent chance a month ago, CME's FedWatch Tool showed.
Back in Asia, Chinese equities on the Shanghai Composite and Shenzhen indexes inched up zero point three per cent each. Factory-gate inflation gathered pace in August and consumer price growth quickened, driven largely by elevated energy costs tied to supply risks from the Middle East war, even as underlying domestic demand remained subdued.
The yuan firmed and hovered at three-year highs.
Asian currencies were mostly higher tracking a weaker US dollar. MSCI's index following EM currencies rose zero point two per cent, touching a new record high.
Indonesian rupiah strengthened zero point seven per cent, to its strongest in nearly four months. Despite the session's gains the currency is among the worst performing currencies in Asia this year.
Elsewhere in South Africa, the economy shrank for the first time in almost two years in the second quarter of 2026, official data showed on Tuesday, dragged down by the Iran war.
Equities index fell one point three per cent, and the currency dropped zero point two per cent.
In emerging Europe, currencies were weaker against the euro.
Polish assets were in focus ahead of the central bank's rate decision later in the session. The National Bank of Poland (NBP) is expected to keep interest rates unchanged at 3.75%, a Reuters poll showed.
The local stocks index declined zero point six per cent, while the zloty dipped zero point two per cent.
Elsewhere, Senegalese bonds nudged higher broadly, with the 2031 dollar bond rising about 0.29 cents on the dollar to be bid at 52.168, its highest since late August.
The country's bonds had suffered sharp losses after a debt restructuring announcement earlier this month. If gains hold, most bonds will have erased those losses.

Title: [UPDATED] Azalina, Asyraf deny attending meeting linked to Negri Sembilan royal dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two top Umno leaders have denied attending a meeting linked to the Negri Sembilan royal dispute.
The duo, Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, said they were not present at any such gathering.
Azalina replied briefly when asked about the matter, saying: "I don't know. I was not there. When he signed it, I was not there, so I don't know."
She was asked to comment on Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim's statement that he was pressured into signing a proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz Munawir as the state ruler.
Asyraf also denied attending the meeting when approached after the same briefing.
"I was not involved. I am only a national leader," he said.
Earlier, Ismail said he had signed the document against his will and under duress, and had lodged a police report at 6pm yesterday.
He said the state government's position was that the document did not comply with the processes and procedures under Article 10 of the state constitution and was therefore invalid and unenforceable.

Title: Parkson signed 15-year lease for RM111mil in Nanchang, China
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parkson Holdings Bhd's 54.97 per cent-owned subsidiary, Parkson Retail Group Ltd (PRGL), has renewed the lease for its retail premises in Nanchang, China for 185 million yuan (RM111 million).
PRGL, which is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, said its indirect wholly-owned subsidiary Jiangxi Parkson Retail Co Ltd had entered into a renewal agreement with Jiangxi Kaimei Development Co Ltd on Sept 9.
The agreement covers a basement-level floor and levels one to four of the premises for 15 years from Jan 1, 2027 to Dec 31, 2041.
Under International Financial Reporting Standard 16 on leases, the premises will be recognised as a right-of-use asset by the PRGL group.
Parkson Holdings said the acquisition of the right-of-use asset is not expected to have a material impact on its earnings for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, or its net assets based on its audited consolidated statement of financial position as at Dec 31, 2025.

Title: Seven years on, Sungai Kim Kim victims win suit against Singaporean directors
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Seven years after toxic waste was illegally dumped into Sungai Kim Kim, 171 victims won their civil suit against a used tyre processing factory, its two Singaporean directors and a lorry driver.
Civil High Court judicial commissioner Manira Mohd Nor ruled today that all 171 plaintiffs had succeeded in their action against P Tech Resources Sdn Bhd, its Singaporean directors Wang Jing Chao, 41, and Yap Yoke Liang, 43, and lorry driver N. Maridass, 42.
The four defendants were ordered to pay RM100,000 in legal costs to the plaintiffs.
However, the plaintiffs failed in their suit against eight other defendants, including the Johor government, then menteri besar the late Datuk Osman Sapian, then state Health and Environment Committee chairman Datuk Sahruddin Jamal, the Johor Environment Department, and the Pasir Gudang Municipal Council, now the Pasir Gudang City Council.
The plaintiffs were ordered to pay RM80,000 in legal costs to the eight defendants.
The chemical pollution occurred on March 13, 2019, affecting more than 2,000 people and forcing the closure of 111 schools in Pasir Gudang.
The incident stemmed from toxic waste dumped into Sungai Kim Kim on March 7, which resulted in 947 people requiring treatment, nine of whom were admitted to the intensive care unit at Hospital Sultan Ismail.
Lawyer Datuk Kamarudin Ahmad, representing all 171 plaintiffs, described the ruling as significant for environmental protection and accountability.
He said the judgment established liability against those responsible for the toxic waste dumping, including the factory, its directors, and the lorry driver.
"This judgment is very important for environmental issues. It should serve as a warning to factories against simply dumping toxic waste into rivers.
"It should also curb the use of unlicensed contractors, lorries and drivers in handling hazardous toxic waste," he said.
The trial, which began in 2022, ran for 20 days and heard testimony from 19 witnesses for the plaintiffs and 12 for the defendants.
Kamarudin said the court would fix a case management date for the assessment of damages.
He said
42 plaintiffs
, comprising students and seven members of the public, were seeking RM30 million in damages, while 129 fishermen were claiming RM3 million for economic losses.
"This was the first phase to determine liability and who was responsible for the Sungai Kim Kim tragedy.
"The next stage will involve the assessment of damages," he said.
For Idham Wazir A. Wahab, 56, the father of one of the worst-affected victims, the judgment brought relief but also disappointment that the claims against the government and local authorities had failed.
His son, Irfan Wafiy Idham Wazir, now 19, suffered from myokymia following the disaster.
"In my view, they (local authorities) also had a responsibility because there were shortcomings in safeguarding the environment in Pasir Gudang," he said.
Idham said Irfan's condition had improved considerably since the disaster.
The teenager, who wants to become a doctor, no longer uses a walking stick, but still experiences pain in his leg and is unable to take part in sports as he once did.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump gave US$45,000 cash gift to 'human printer' aide: US media
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump gave his executive assistant Natalie Harp a US$45,000 cash gift, US media reported Tuesday.
Two other White House employees, Margo Martin and Chamberlain Harris, received similar amounts, according to the Washington Post.
The three women described the payments as "Cash Gift for Holidays," the Washington Post reported, citing financial disclosure forms.
Harp has been a near-constant presence at Trump's side in his second term, sometimes typing out social media posts for him and printing out information, a role that has seen her dubbed the "human printer."
She earns US$150,000 a year in her role as the special assistant and executive assistant to the president, according to an annual report to Congress.
A White House spokesperson defended the gifts, citing Trump's "longstanding practice of giving Christmas gifts to people in his orbit, including at times employees and aides."
They said the gifts were unrelated to any of the individuals' duties, making them "entirely permissible under relevant legal and ethical standards."

Title: Negri Sembilan Umno urges swift resolution to issue surrounding ruler's position
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan Umno has called for a speedy resolution to the issue surrounding the position of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Its liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said he had no knowledge of rumours that Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim would resign amid the issue.
"As the state Umno chief, I hope this can be resolved as soon as possible.
"I don't know (about the resignation rumours). I'm not in the system anymore. I am no longer a member of the state administration.
"We learnt about what has happened over the past few days through media reports," he told reporters after attending the Umno presidential briefing at the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here today.
Asked about Ismail signing the Instrument of Proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz, Jalaluddin declined to comment further.
"I have no comment on what the menteri besar has said in his statement. That was his statement," he said.
Earlier today, Ismail claimed he had been
forced to sign the document
and said he lodged a police report at about 6pm yesterday to allow the authorities to investigate.
He said the state government considered the document invalid, unconstitutional and unenforceable as it did not comply with the processes and procedures under Article 10 of the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959.
